source_text: Non est libidini satis malis suis uti praesentibus , nisi suum de spectaculo faciant in quo etiam aetas superior errauerat. non licet, inquam, adesse christianis fidelibus, non licet omnino nec illis quos ad delinimenta aurium ad omnes ubique Graecia instructos suis uanis artibus mittit. clangores tubae bellicos alter imitatur raucos, alter lugubres sonos spiritu tibiam inflante moderatur, alter cum choris et cum hominis canora uoce contendens spiritu suo quem de uisceribus suis superioribus nitens hauserat tibiarum foramina modulatur: nunc effuso et nunc intus recluso ac represso nunc certis foraminibus emisso atque in aerem profuso, item in articulos sonum frangens, loqui digitis elaborat, ingratus artifici qui linguam dedit. quid loquar comicas inutiles curas, quid illas magnas tragicae uocis insanias, quid neruos cum clamore commissos ? haec etiam si non essent simulacris dicata, obeunda tamen et spectanda non essent christianis fidelibus: quoniam etsi non habebant crimen, habent in ae maximam et parum congruentem fidelibus uanitatem.
thought_title: The vanity of stage music and plays
orientation: Novatian is still describing the stage plays, now turning from their obscene dancing to their music and tragic performances, and concluding that even apart from idolatry they are vain and unfit for faithful Christians.
pass_a_gloss: It is not enough for lust to use its own present evils, unless it makes its own from the public show that in which even an earlier age had erred. It is not permitted, I say, for faithful Christians to be present, it is not permitted at all, not even for those whom Greece, instructed in all places for the soothing of ears, sends with her empty arts. One imitates the hoarse warlike blasts of the trumpet, another controls mournful sounds with his breath as the pipe blows, another, contending with choruses and with the singing voice of a man, with his own breath which he had drawn, straining from his upper inward parts, plays the holes of the pipes: now with breath poured out and now shut in and pressed back within, now sent out through certain holes and poured into the air, likewise breaking the sound into notes, he works to speak with his fingers, ungrateful to the craftsman who gave him a tongue. Why should I speak of the useless cares of comedy, why of those great frenzies of the tragic voice, why of strings joined with shouting? These things, even if they were not dedicated to idols, still should not be attended and watched by faithful Christians: since even if they did not have guilt, they have in themselves the greatest vanity and one little suited to the faithful.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'public shows' for spectacula; here the singular refers to the whole institution of the stage show.
The glossary fixes this rendering for the baptized believer whose profession obliges avoidance.
uanitas is the glossary term for vanity or emptiness; 'empty arts' keeps the root sense of uanis while fitting the musical context.
simulacra are the idol images; 'dedicated to idols' preserves the cultic force of dicata.
The glossary requires 'vanity' for uanitas, the emptiness of spectacles apart from idolatry.

pass_b_english: Lust is not satisfied with using its present evils; it must also make the public show its own, in which even an earlier age went astray. I say it is not permitted for faithful Christians to attend—not permitted at all, even for those whom Greece, trained in empty arts, sends everywhere to soothe the ears. One imitates the hoarse blasts of the war trumpet; another shapes mournful sounds by breathing into the pipe; another contends with choirs and with the human voice in song, and with the breath he has drawn from deep within his chest modulates the holes of the pipes—now releasing it, now holding it back and pressing it in, now sending it out through certain holes and pouring it into the air, then breaking the sound into notes, laboring to speak with his fingers, ungrateful to the Maker who gave him a tongue. Why should I speak of the useless follies of comedy, of those great frenzies of the tragic voice, of strings joined with shouting? Even if these things were not dedicated to idols, they still should not be attended or watched by faithful Christians, because even if they held no crime, they hold in themselves the greatest vanity, and one hardly fitting for the faithful.

last_rejected.why: Latin says “delinimenta aurium” (offences/defilements of the ears), not soothing; the English reverses the sense.
last_rejected.ruling: delinimenta means soothing/softening; related to delinio, not defilement. Translation is correct.

problems.why: Section 7 describes the same instrument type as section 2's list but uses a different English term.

edits.old: modulates the holes of the pipes
edits.new: modulates the holes of the flutes

fixed: The source uses 'tibiarum' (pipes/flutes) in this section, and the brief's glossary does not mandate a specific term. The confirmed problem asks for consistency with section 2's list, which uses 'flutes'. I changed 'pipes' to 'flutes' to match.
